lesson_name: Where in the world are tropical rainforests?

photos.subject: A park or open woodland in Britain with large oak trees and grass, on an ordinary day
photos.pedagogical_constraint: This is our own kind of place, the British weather the lesson starts from; it must look like Britain, not somewhere tropical.
photos.teaching_requirement: Children see the kind of trees that grow in Britain's weather, as the starting point for the idea that weather decides what grows.
load_bearing_evidence: large oak or similar broadleaf trees
an ordinary British park or woodland scene

generation_prompt.physical_state: A British park with large oak trees in full leaf and grass, mild daylight.
generation_prompt.text_rule: no readable text, labels, logos or branding
generation_prompt.composition: A wide landscape view of the park with the trees clearly visible.

photos.subject: A hot sandy desert such as the Sahara, with bare sand and only a few small, tough plants
photos.pedagogical_constraint: The desert is shown as a biome where it hardly ever rains, so it must look dry, with almost no plants.
photos.teaching_requirement: Children see that very little can grow where it hardly ever rains, the contrast that shows weather decides what grows.
load_bearing_evidence: very few, small plants or none

generation_prompt.physical_state: A hot sandy desert under a clear sky, with bare dunes and one or two small dry shrubs.
must_avoid: camels or people filling the frame
generation_prompt.text_rule: no readable text, labels, logos or branding
generation_prompt.composition: A wide landscape view of the desert.

photos.subject: Inside or at the edge of a dense tropical rainforest, with huge tall trees packed close together and thick green leaves
photos.pedagogical_constraint: Shown beside the desert as the other biome, and on the word card for biome: it must look hot, wet and crowded with tall green trees.
photos.teaching_requirement: Children see that where it is hot and rains nearly every day, huge trees grow close together and stay green.
load_bearing_evidence: a damp, misty or wet look

generation_prompt.physical_state: A dense tropical rainforest with very tall trees close together, thick green leaves and a little mist.
must_avoid: a single tree on its own
generation_prompt.text_rule: no readable text, labels, logos or branding
generation_prompt.composition: A landscape view showing the height and closeness of the trees.

photos.subject: A clear illustration of the Sun's rays reaching the Earth: rays hit the middle of the globe straight on and reach the top and bottom at a slant, spread out
photos.pedagogical_constraint: Shows it happening: the Sun's rays hitting the middle of the Earth straight on and spreading out at a slant towards the top and the bottom, so the middle gets the strongest sunshine.
photos.teaching_requirement: Children see why it is hot all year near the Equator: the sunshine there is the most direct and strongest.
load_bearing_evidence: the Sun on one side with parallel rays coming from it
rays hitting the middle of the Earth straight on
rays reaching the top and bottom of the Earth at a slant and spread over a wider area
the Earth drawn as a globe with land and sea
photos.fallback_note: If no picture can be made, the slide shows the rainforest photograph as a stand-in and the teacher is told; a torch shone at a ball shows the same thing live.

generation_prompt.physical_state: Parallel rays travel from the Sun to the Earth; the band around the middle of the Earth faces the rays directly, while the rays reach the top and bottom at a shallow angle and spread out.
must_avoid: the Sun drawn touching or overlapping the Earth
generation_prompt.text_rule: no readable text, letters or labels
generation_prompt.composition: A simple, clear science illustration on a plain background, landscape, with the Sun on the left and the Earth as a globe on the right.

photos.subject: The Amazon rainforest in Brazil seen from above, with the Amazon River or one of its big branches winding through endless forest
photos.pedagogical_constraint: This is the real Amazon, shown on the slide that locates it; it must be a real photograph of the Amazon.
photos.teaching_requirement: Children see how huge the Amazon rainforest is, with its river winding through it, while they learn where it is.
load_bearing_evidence: forest stretching as far as the eye can see
a wide river winding through the forest
photos.fallback_note: A made picture would claim to show the real Amazon when it does not. Without the photograph, the map on the same slide still shows where the Amazon is.
